title: Injective modules on a ringed site restrict surjectively along monomorphisms
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of commutative unital rings on it. Work in a common universe containing the objects, arrows, covering index sets, ring values and module values [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $I$ be an injective object [def-sp-injective-resolutions] of the category $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For every monomorphism $m:W\to T$ in $\mathcal C$, the restriction homomorphism $I(T)\to I(W)$ is surjective. No subcanonicality, covering property of $m$, or injectivity of the underlying abelian sheaf is assumed.

source.place: Tag 093X, label lemma-restriction-along-monomorphism-surjective, lines 1962-2009; Stacks conventions.tex line 51: rings are commutative with 1

proof.text: For each object $U$, put $P_U=\mathcal O[h_U]$, the presheaf $V\mapsto\bigoplus_{\varphi:V\to U}\mathcal O(V)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-free-yoneda-presheaf-module], and put $L_U=P_U^\#$ using [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. The adjunction in the latter statement and the evaluation bijection in the former give $\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)}(L_U,F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{PMod}(\mathcal O)}(P_U,F)\cong F(U)$ for every module sheaf $F$. Explicitly, a sheaf morphism $b:L_U\to F$ corresponds to the value at $e_{\mathrm{id}_U}$ of the presheaf map $\widetilde b:P_U\to F$ obtained by precomposing with the sheafification unit. Conversely, $s\in F(U)$ determines the presheaf map $e_\varphi\mapsto F(\varphi)(s)$ and its unique extension to $L_U$. The common-universe hypothesis ensures these direct sums and sheafifications belong to the category in which $I$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 093X, lemma-restriction-along-monomorphism-surjective, first paragraph; sites-modules.tex Tag 03DI, equation-map-lower-shriek-OU-into-module; Remark 03EJ and module sheafification Tag 03CY

proof.text: Define $a:P_W\to P_T$ at $V$ by the $\mathcal O(V)$-linear map $a_V(e_\varphi)=e_{m\circ\varphi}$ for $\varphi:V\to W$. This is a morphism of module presheaves: for $g:V\prime\to V$ and $r\in\mathcal O(V)$, restricting $a_V(r e_\varphi)$ gives $\mathcal O(g)(r)e_{m\circ\varphi\circ g}$, which is also $a_{V\prime}$ applied to the restriction of $r e_\varphi$. Finite sums of these generators exhaust $P_W(V)$, so the equality proves naturality on every section.

source.place: Tag 093X, lemma-restriction-along-monomorphism-surjective, second paragraph: map between the displayed direct-sum presheaves

proof.text: Since $m$ is monic, $\varphi\mapsto m\circ\varphi$ is injective on $\operatorname{Hom}(V,W)$ for every $V$. For a finitely supported tuple $x=(x_\varphi)$, the coefficient of $a_V(x)$ at $m\circ\varphi$ is exactly $x_\varphi$, because no other index has this image. Thus $a_V(x)=0$ forces every $x_\varphi=0$, proving $a_V$ injective. Consequently $a$ is monic as a presheaf morphism: if $a\circ b=a\circ c$, evaluate at each $V$, cancel the injective $a_V$ on each section, and obtain $b=c$. This uses no claim that the componentwise coefficient-recovery maps are natural.

source.place: Tag 093X, lemma-restriction-along-monomorphism-surjective, last two sentences: the monomorphism gives injectivity on direct sums

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-sheafification-exact] to the given ringed site. Sheafification preserves finite limits, and hence monomorphisms, so the monomorphism $a$ from Step 3 gives a monomorphism $a^\#:L_W\hookrightarrow L_T$ of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules. This is sheafification for the actual sheaf of rings $\mathcal O$, rather than sheafification for modules over a fixed constant ring.

source.place: Tag 093X, lemma-restriction-along-monomorphism-surjective, final sentence; sites-modules.tex Tag 03EI, lemma-sheafification-exact

proof.text: The category $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ is abelian for the small site and common universe by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. By the definition of injectivity in [def-sp-injective-resolutions], precomposition with $a^\#$ is surjective from $\operatorname{Hom}(L_T,I)$ to $\operatorname{Hom}(L_W,I)$. To identify this map, take $t\in I(T)$ and its morphism $b_t:L_T\to I$ from Step 1. The corresponding presheaf map sends $e_\psi$ to $I(\psi)(t)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-free-yoneda-presheaf-module]. Naturality of the sheafification unit shows that the presheaf map associated to $b_t\circ a^\#$ is $\widetilde b_t\circ a$. Evaluating it at $e_{\mathrm{id}_W}$ gives $\widetilde b_{t,W}(e_m)=I(m)(t)$. Therefore the surjective Hom map is precisely $I(T)\to I(W)$. For each $s\in I(W)$, extend its map $L_W\to I$ across $a^\#$ and evaluate the extension at $e_{\mathrm{id}_T}$ to obtain $t$ with $I(m)(t)=s$.
